name: Veterinary clinics (category guide)
summary: AVS-licensed vets for post-import pets — licence clocks, emergency vs GP clinics, and why relocation agents are not your ongoing clinic.
body: After CAPQ and the relocation agent handoff, you still need a neighbourhood veterinary clinic for vaccines, parasite control, and emergencies. Confirm the practice is licensed under NParks / Animal & Veterinary Service (AVS) rules — Facebook ‘house-call only’ vendors are a recurring risk. Budget for higher cash fees than many home countries; pet insurance sold overseas often excludes Singapore clinics or waits out pre-existing conditions. Ask about after-hours coverage before the first fever at 11pm — not every GP vet runs a 24-hour emergency bench. Keep import vaccination and rabies-serology originals; clinics will not reinvent CAPQ paperwork from memory. Licensing and sterilisation rules for dogs/cats sit with AVS and your town council / condo by-laws — clinic advice does not override estate pet clauses. Pair this directory entry with the pet-relocation category guide for import, and with daily-life pet guidance for housing and transit. This is a category guide, not a ranked vet list. Family ops note: human varicella weeks are not pet-care holidays — keep vaccine and boarding bookings off the same calendar day as GP clearance visits. Family ops note: human exclusion weeks still need pet-care coverage owners — do not invent “the helper will walk the dog” folklore when rest-day collisions stack with scarlet-fever coverage.
